questions.group: Establish what you are looking at
questions.q: Is this running your production software, or a demo build?
questions.good: A straight yes or no. A demo build is fine; not knowing is not.

questions.group: Establish what you are looking at
questions.q: How many of these are in production today, and at how many sites?
questions.good: Two numbers. A large unit count across one site is a different risk from a small count across many.

questions.group: Establish what you are looking at
questions.q: Is the demo running on a fixed route, or is it deciding where to go?
questions.good: Fixed-path and free-roaming systems make different demands on your floor and your building.

questions.q: That rate, per what, and measured over how long?
questions.good: Per station, per robot, per person, and a window longer than an hour. Vagueness here is the answer.

questions.q: Does the clock include travel, charging, exceptions and idle time?
questions.good: Yes, with the definition. A rate measured only while picking is not one you can staff to.

questions.q: Will you put that number in a pilot contract as an acceptance test?
questions.good: Yes, or a clear reason why not. This is the single most informative question on the sheet.

questions.q: Which safety standard does this conform to, and which edition?
questions.good: A named standard and year. See the standards card below for what each one actually covers.

questions.q: Who does the task-based risk assessment, and when do I see it?
questions.good: Before commissioning, produced by the integrator with your people involved.

questions.q: Who owns the data this system generates in my building?
questions.good: A clear answer. In at least one major filed agreement, the vendor owns it.

questions.q: What does the software license cost after year one, and is it transferable?
questions.good: A number, and whether you can sell the site with a working system in it.

questions.q: Can I have a reference site running my SKU profile, not your best one?
questions.good: A name and a phone number, or an honest no.

groups: Establish what you are looking at

standards.what: Safety Standard for Driverless, Automatic Guided Industrial Vehicles and Automated Functions of Manned Industrial Vehicles. Effective 16 Dec 2025.
standards.note: Free on request from ITSDF, in exchange for your name, company and email and an agreement not to resell it.
standards.quote: Copies of these standards are available for free upon request

standards.what: Industrial mobile robot safety. Part 1 covers the robot, part 2 the system and application, part 3 the use of it.
standards.note: Part 3 is the operator's part, published 2026. Asking whether deployment guidance conforms to it is a fair question.

standards.what: Performance test methods for robotics and autonomous systems: navigation, docking, obstacle detection, communication, terminology.
standards.note: Do not cite F45 as a safety credential. Its own navigation test method points you at the safety standards instead.
standards.quote: This standard does not purport to address all of the safety concerns, if any, associated with its use. Safety standards such as ANSI/ITSDF B56.5, ISO 3691-4:2020, or other safety standards should be followed.

standards.what: European rules for commissioning, hand-over and testing installations with storage and retrieval machines. Free download.
standards.note: Useful as a model for a contractual acceptance test. It tells you to agree the target before signing, not what the target should be.
standards.quote: The availability of the installation should be specified, at the latest, before signing the contract with the customer.
